what: Arguments each client refuses before anything is sent, and what it says. The message is the same in all three, in each language's names (user_id / userId), except where a row says how the idioms differ; rust_says is Rust's words where they differ from Python's.

cases.python_says: user_id must be a non-blank string; got "  ". Omit it to use the client's default store, or pass a real store id — anything else would silently write into the default store.
cases.typescript_says: userId must be a non-blank string; got "  ". Omit it to use the client's default store, or pass a real store id — anything else would silently write into the default store.

cases.python_says: user_id must be a non-blank string; got 5. Omit it to use the client's default store, or pass a real store id — anything else would silently write into the default store.
cases.typescript_says: userId must be a non-blank string; got 5. Omit it to use the client's default store, or pass a real store id — anything else would silently write into the default store.

cases.python_says: created_at must be a datetime with a time zone or an RFC 3339 time with Z or a ±hh:mm offset, such as 2026-05-02T09:00:00Z (a date alone, a time with no offset, and a space or a small t in place of the T are refused), got "2024-03-01".
cases.typescript_says: createdAt must be a Date or an RFC 3339 time with Z or a ±hh:mm offset, such as 2026-05-02T09:00:00Z (a date alone, a time with no offset, and a space or a small t in place of the T are refused), got "2024-03-01".
cases.differs_by_idiom: a datetime in Python, a Date in TypeScript
cases.rust_says: created_at must be an RFC 3339 time with Z or a ±hh:mm offset, such as 2026-05-02T09:00:00Z (a date alone, a time with no offset, and a space or a small t in place of the T are refused), got "2024-03-01".

cases.python_says: user_speaker is for add_turn: it names a side of a turn. On add, name who said it with speaker=.
cases.typescript_says: user_speaker is for addTurn: it names a side of a turn. On add, name who said it in metadata.speaker.
cases.differs_by_idiom: speaker= in Python, metadata.speaker in TypeScript
cases.rust_says: user_speaker is for add_turn_opts: it names a side of a turn. On add, name who said it in metadata.speaker.
